children.title: Distributed Optimization Complexity Measures
children.top_down_role: Cost models distinguishing computation, communication, synchronization, and total work.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathfrak A\) be a distributed algorithm, \(I\) an instance, \(\varepsilon>0\) an accuracy target, and \(\tau\) a terminating execution whose output satisfies a declared certificate \(C_I(\tau)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition treats distributed complexity as a resource vector so computation, communication, synchronization, volume, and elapsed time are not conflated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a terminating execution \(\tau\), define its resource vector \(R(\tau)=(N_{\mathrm{orc}},N_{\mathrm{rnd}},N_{\mathrm{msg}},N_{\mathrm{bit}},D_{\mathrm{sync}},T_{\mathrm{par}})\in[0,\infty]^6\). The worst-case distributed complexity of \(\mathfrak A\) on an instance class \(\mathcal I\) is the componentwise supremum of the resources required by executions that first produce an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate output. A scalar complexity is defined only after specifying a monotone cost functional \(w\), giving \(\mathcal C_w(\mathfrak A,\mathcal I,\varepsilon)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\sup_\omega w(R(\tau_{I,\omega,\varepsilon}))\), where \(\omega\) represents admissible randomness or schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed complexity is the vector of resources consumed before an accuracy certificate is reached. Its coordinates separately count local oracle work, sequential communication rounds, messages, encoded bits, synchronization depth, and parallel elapsed time. Worst-case complexity takes the supremum over the declared instance class and admissible executions. A scalar total cost is meaningful only after resource weights or a cost model are specified.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The attainable resource set \(\mathcal R_\varepsilon=\{R(\tau):C_I(\tau)\le\varepsilon\}\) retains tradeoffs that a single weighted scalar may hide.
special_cases_latex: Round complexity is obtained by \(w(R)=N_{\mathrm{rnd}}\); bit complexity uses \(w(R)=N_{\mathrm{bit}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Algorithms can be incomparable when neither resource vector componentwise dominates the other.
boundary_notes: Wall-clock time requires a hardware and latency model and cannot be inferred solely from operation counts.
Expected, high-probability, and worst-case complexities are distinct conventions.

notation.meaning: Resource vector of execution \(\tau\).
Declared monotone scalarization of resource use.

children.title: Distributed Local Oracle Complexity
children.top_down_role: Local derivative, subgradient, proximal, or function-value costs.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Oracle Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed distributed execution, local oracle complexity records either the largest per-agent query count or the total query count needed to reach the declared accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a distributed algorithm execution, an oracle class, and an accuracy criterion \(E(x)\leq\varepsilon\). Let \(q_i(t)\in\mathbb N_0\) be the number of declared local oracle calls made by agent \(i\in\{1,n\}\) through iteration \(t\). Define the execution-level worst-agent and aggregate local oracle costs by \[Q_{\max}(\varepsilon):=\inf_{t:E(x^t)\leq\varepsilon}\max_{1\leq i\leq n}q_i(t),\qquad Q_{\Sigma}(\varepsilon):=\inf_{t:E(x^t)\leq\varepsilon}\sum_{i=1}^n q_i(t).\] If no qualifying iterate exists, the corresponding value is \(+\infty\). The first quantity measures worst-agent local work, and the second measures total network-wide oracle work. Query types with materially different costs are counted separately or combined through an explicit cost model.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm execution, error criterion \(E\), outputs \(x^t\), and target \(\varepsilon\) are specified.
The permitted oracle responses and their counting convention are fixed.
\(q_i(t)\in\mathbb N_0\) counts agent \(i\)'s oracle calls through iteration \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\max}(\varepsilon)\) and \(Q_{\Sigma}(\varepsilon)\) quantify worst-agent and aggregate execution-level local oracle costs, respectively.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-agent and aggregate counts of local information requests needed for accuracy.

notation.meaning: Number of local oracle calls made by agent i through iteration t.
Worst-agent local oracle cost.
Aggregate local oracle cost.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Agent \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) accesses its private function or constraint data only through an oracle \(\mathcal O_i\), which may return a function value, gradient, subgradient, proximal point, stochastic sample, or another declared response.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This measure counts local information queries independently of communication and local arithmetic not charged by the oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an execution \(\tau\), let \(q_i(\tau)\) be the number of calls to \(\mathcal O_i\) made before an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate certificate is produced. The aggregate local oracle cost is \(N_{\mathrm{orc}}^{\Sigma}(\tau)=\sum_{i=1}^n q_i(\tau)\), while the parallel-depth oracle cost is \(N_{\mathrm{orc}}^{\max}(\tau)=\max_i q_i(\tau)\). For algorithm \(\mathfrak A\) and instance class \(\mathcal I\), the corresponding worst-case complexity is the supremum of the selected count over all admissible instances and executions reaching the target. Different oracle response types must be counted separately or assigned declared weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local oracle complexity counts private-data queries made by agents before the required accuracy is certified. The aggregate convention sums calls over agents; the parallel-depth convention takes the maximum per-agent count. Function-value, derivative, subgradient, proximal, and stochastic calls are distinct resources unless an explicit weighting combines them.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A typed query vector \((q_i^{\mathrm{val}},q_i^{\mathrm{grad}},q_i^{\mathrm{prox}},q_i^{\mathrm{stoch}})\) is equivalent to a scalar count only after weights are fixed.
special_cases_latex: If every synchronous iteration makes one gradient call at every agent, then after \(K\) iterations the aggregate count is \(nK\) and the per-agent depth is \(K\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Equal round complexity does not imply equal oracle complexity when agents perform multiple local steps between communications.
boundary_notes: Communication, encoding, and arbitrary local arithmetic are excluded unless the oracle model charges them.
Batch size must be declared when one stochastic call can process multiple samples.

children.title: Distributed Communication-Round Complexity
children.top_down_role: Sequential network exchanges required to reach an accuracy target.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Communication-Round Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication-round complexity is the minimum number of sequential neighbor-exchange stages needed to satisfy a declared accuracy and success criterion, regardless of intervening local computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a synchronous graph model and an accuracy predicate \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon(x)\) that incorporates the selected deterministic, expected, or high-probability success convention. One communication round permits every agent to send messages to its current neighbors and receive the corresponding messages before the next adaptive exchange. If \(x^R\) is the distributed output after \(R\in\mathbb N_0\) rounds, define \[R(\varepsilon):=\inf\left\{R\in\mathbb N_0:\mathcal A_\varepsilon(x^R)\text{ holds}\right\}.\] If the set is empty, \(R(\varepsilon):=+\infty\). Local computations between two exchanges do not increase this count, whereas \(k\) sequential consensus or gossip exchanges count as \(k\) rounds.
assumptions_latex: Communication is organized into synchronous neighbor-exchange rounds.
The graph model and accuracy predicate \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon\) are fixed.
The predicate includes the selected deterministic, expected, or high-probability success convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R(\varepsilon)\) is the minimum number of sequential communication rounds after which \(\mathcal A_\varepsilon(x^R)\) holds, or \(+\infty\) if no such round exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential network-exchange rounds required to attain a declared accuracy.

notation.meaning: Communication-round cost at accuracy epsilon.
Distributed output after R communication rounds.
Accuracy predicate including the chosen success convention.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let communication occur on an admissible graph or time-varying graph sequence. In one round, each agent may form messages from its current local information, transmit them over simultaneously available edges, receive that round's messages, and update its state.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The measure counts causal network depth, not message volume, bit length, local computation, or physical elapsed time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A communication round is one synchronous causal layer of neighbor-to-neighbor message exchange. For execution \(\tau\), let \(N_{\mathrm{rnd}}(\tau)\) be the number of such layers before the first output satisfying the declared \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy certificate. The communication-round complexity of algorithm \(\mathfrak A\) over \(\mathcal I\) is \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{rnd}}(\mathfrak A,\mathcal I,\varepsilon)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}\sup_\omega N_{\mathrm{rnd}}(\tau_{I,\omega,\varepsilon})\). For asynchronous executions, a round surrogate must be defined explicitly, for example as communication depth in the event-dependency directed acyclic graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication-round complexity is the worst-case number of sequential network-exchange layers required before the accuracy target is reached. Transmissions within the same causal layer count as one round even if many messages are sent. Asynchronous systems require an explicit causal-depth or epoch convention.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under a synchronous model with one mixing operation per iteration, iteration count and communication-round count coincide.
Communication depth is the length of the longest chain of message-dependent exchange events in a causal execution graph.
special_cases_latex: Performing \(s\) consecutive consensus exchanges per optimization iteration costs \(sK\) rounds after \(K\) iterations.
immediate_consequences_latex: Round complexity can remain unchanged when messages are enlarged, so it does not control communication volume.
boundary_notes: A broadcast counts according to the declared network primitive; it must not silently be treated as one neighbor round.
Idle time and link latency are excluded from an abstract round count.

notation.meaning: Sequential communication depth before certification.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Message, coordinate, and bit communication costs
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a terminating distributed execution \(\tau\), let \(M(\tau)\) be its multiset of directed transmissions. Each message \(m\in M(\tau)\) has an encoded length \(\ell(m)\in\mathbb N\) bits and may contain \(d(m)\) scalar coordinates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This taxonomy concerns communication volume and keeps it distinct from sequential communication depth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The message complexity is \(N_{\mathrm{msg}}(\tau)=|M(\tau)|\). The coordinate complexity is \(N_{\mathrm{coord}}(\tau)=\sum_{m\in M(\tau)}d(m)\). The bit complexity is \(N_{\mathrm{bit}}(\tau)=\sum_{m\in M(\tau)}\ell(m)\), including declared headers or metadata when the model charges them. For a class of instances and executions, each worst-case complexity is the supremum of the corresponding count before an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate certificate is reached. Equivalence between coordinate and bit counts requires a fixed encoding precision; without it, transmitting one real coordinate has no finite intrinsic bit cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Message complexity counts transmissions, coordinate complexity sums transmitted scalar entries, and bit complexity sums encoded lengths. These are different measures: a single message may contain many coordinates, and a coordinate may require a variable number of bits. Worst-case costs are measured up to the first certified accurate output.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If every coordinate is encoded using exactly \(b\) bits and headers are excluded, then \(N_{\mathrm{bit}}=bN_{\mathrm{coord}}\).
special_cases_latex: Sending one dense vector in \(\mathbb R^d\) on every directed edge in every round gives coordinate cost \(d\) times the number of directed edge transmissions.
immediate_consequences_latex: A round-efficient algorithm need not be bit-efficient, and compression can lower bit cost without lowering round count.
boundary_notes: Infinite-precision real messages do not define finite bit complexity.
Broadcast accounting must state whether one physical broadcast or one transmission per recipient is charged.

notation.meaning: Multiset of directed messages transmitted during execution \(\tau\).
Encoded bit length of message \(m\).

Message-Count Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Message-count complexity is the worst-case number of completed edgewise message transmissions over all declared instances and admissible executions before an accuracy-qualified output is produced; an unsuccessful execution has infinite count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an admissible execution transcript \(\tau\), define \[M(\tau)=\sum_{e\in\tau}\mathbf{1}\{e\text{ is a completed message transmission}\}.\] For a distributed algorithm \(A\), instance class \(\mathcal I\), accuracy predicate \(P_\varepsilon(x;I)\), and admissible-execution set \(\Omega_A(I)\), define \[M_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I,\,\omega\in\Omega_A(I)}M(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega)).\] Here \(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega)\) ends when an output satisfying \(P_\varepsilon\) is first produced. Its message count is \(+\infty\) if no such output is produced. Each multicast is counted once per receiving edge, and retransmissions are counted separately.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has a specified termination rule and accuracy predicate \(P_\varepsilon\).
\(\mathcal I\) is the declared instance class, and \(\Omega_A(I)\) is the declared class of admissible executions on \(I\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bit-Communication Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bit-communication complexity is the worst-case total charged binary length over all declared instances and admissible executions before an accuracy-qualified output is produced; an unsuccessful execution has infinite cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell(e)\in\mathbb N_0\) be the complete encoded length, in bits, of communication event \(e\), including every header charged by the declared model. For a transcript \(\tau\), define \[B(\tau)=\sum_{e\in\tau}\ell(e).\] For algorithm \(A\), instance class \(\mathcal I\), and admissible-execution set \(\Omega_A(I)\), define \[B_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I,\,\omega\in\Omega_A(I)}B(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega)).\] The transcript ends when an output satisfying the declared \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy predicate is first produced, and an execution that produces no such output has value \(+\infty\). Preshared random seeds cost zero only when the declared model makes them free; otherwise their communicated descriptions contribute to \(B\).
assumptions_latex: \(\ell(e)\) is fixed by a declared binary encoding and accounting convention.
\(\mathcal I\) and each admissible-execution set \(\Omega_A(I)\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts encoded payload and protocol bits transmitted before attaining accuracy.

notation.meaning: Charged encoded length of communication event e in bits.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Transmission Volume
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate volume is the worst-case total number of scalar entries carried across receiving edges, irrespective of their encoding precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each communication event \(e\) carries an encoded vector whose decoded payload exposes a set \(S_e\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d_e\}\) of transmitted scalar coordinates. Define the coordinate-transmission volume of transcript \(\tau\) by \[V_{\mathrm{coord}}(\tau)=\sum_{e\in\tau}|S_e|.\] The worst-case volume for algorithm \(A\) is \[V_A(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}V_{\mathrm{coord}}(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon)).\] A coordinate sent to several neighbors is charged once per receiving edge; metadata and coordinate precision are excluded and must instead be charged by a bit measure.
assumptions_latex: Each message has a declared decoded coordinate support \(S_e\).
A multicast payload is represented by one event for each receiving edge.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts transmitted scalar coordinates independently of their bit precision.

notation.meaning: Set of scalar coordinate positions transmitted by event e.
Total coordinate-transmission volume of transcript tau.

knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Precision Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precision is fixed, accuracy-dependent finite, or ideal exact-real according to whether the maximum encoded payload length stays bounded as accuracy tightens.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a family of encoders \(Q_\varepsilon\), let \(b(\varepsilon)=\sup_z\ell(Q_\varepsilon(z))\) over admissible payloads \(z\). The family has fixed precision if \(\sup_{0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0}b(\varepsilon)<\infty\); it has accuracy-dependent finite precision if every \(b(\varepsilon)<\infty\) but \(\sup_{0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0}b(\varepsilon)=\infty\); and it is an exact-real regime if payloads are ideal real words whose charged length is not represented by finite \(b(\varepsilon)\). Bit-complexity comparisons are meaningful only within the same regime and encoding convention.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_\varepsilon\) and its binary length function \(\ell\) are specified for every target \(0<\varepsilon\leq\varepsilon_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies communication models by how message precision may depend on target accuracy.

notation.meaning: Encoder used at target accuracy epsilon.
Maximum encoded payload length at accuracy epsilon.

children.title: Distributed Wall-Clock and Parallel-Time Complexity
children.top_down_role: Latency-aware cost incorporating concurrency and synchronization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Represent an execution \(\tau\) by a directed acyclic event graph \(H_\tau=(V_\tau,A_\tau)\). Vertices are local computations, transmissions, receptions, or synchronization events; arcs encode causal precedence. Each event \(v\) has duration \(c(v)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This model captures concurrency, heterogeneous communication delays, and synchronization; it is distinct from aggregate work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The latency-aware parallel time of execution \(\tau\) is its weighted critical-path length \(T_{\mathrm{par}}(\tau)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P(H_\tau)}\sum_{v\in P}c(v)\), where \(\mathcal P(H_\tau)\) is the set of directed causal paths ending at the first event that exposes an \(\varepsilon\)-accurate output. Its worst-case complexity is the supremum over the declared instance, schedule, delay, and randomness class. For a bulk-synchronous model with round latency \(L_k\) and between-round critical local work \(W_k\), this specializes to \(T_{\mathrm{par}}=\sum_{k=1}^{K}(L_k+W_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Latency-aware parallel-time complexity is the duration of the longest causal chain leading to an accurate output. Independent work runs concurrently and therefore contributes through a maximum rather than a sum. A synchronous specialization adds per-round communication latency and the critical local work between barriers.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With unlimited processors and deterministic event durations, the weighted critical path is the earliest completion time permitted by the precedence constraints.
special_cases_latex: For constant round latency \(L\), constant critical work \(W\), and \(K\) barriers, \(T_{\mathrm{par}}=K(L+W)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Reducing total work need not reduce parallel time if the critical path is unchanged.
boundary_notes: Contention, queueing, failures, and bandwidth limits are included only when represented in event durations or precedence constraints.
This is a model-based time, not a machine-independent operation count.

notation.meaning: Causal event graph of execution \(\tau\).
Duration assigned to event \(v\).
Directed causal paths leading to the certified output.

knowledge_statements.title: Latency-aware critical-path complexity
Wall-Clock Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wall-clock complexity is the worst-case modeled elapsed time over all declared instances and admissible executions until an accuracy-qualified output first becomes available; a nonterminating execution has infinite time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an admissible timed execution \(\tau_A(I,psilon;\omega)\), let \(t_0(I,\omega)\) be its start time and \(t_{\mathrm{out}}(I,\omega)\) the first time an admissible processor produces an output satisfying the declared \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy predicate. Define \[T_{\mathrm{wall}}(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega))=t_{\mathrm{out}}(I,\omega)-t_0(I,\omega),\] and \[T_A^{\mathrm{wall}}(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I,\,\omega\in\Omega_A(I)}T_{\mathrm{wall}}(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon;\omega)).\] Computation, queueing, transmission, latency, waiting, and synchronization contribute according to their actual overlap in the declared machine and scheduler model. If no qualifying output is produced, the execution time is \(+\infty\).
assumptions_latex: The machine, network, scheduler, and event-duration model are fixed.
\(\Omega_A(I)\) specifies all admissible executions of \(A\) on \(I\).
The first qualifying output time \(t_{\mathrm{out}}\) is observable under the declared termination rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures elapsed physical time under an explicit computation, communication, and scheduling model.

notation.meaning: Elapsed time of one timed execution.
Worst-case wall-clock complexity.
Declared set of admissible executions of A on instance I.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel-Time Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel-time complexity is the worst-case weighted critical-path length of the execution, assuming causally independent operations can run concurrently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent an execution by a directed acyclic graph \(D_\tau=(V_\tau,E_\tau)\), where vertices are primitive computation or communication operations, edges encode causal precedence, and \(w(v)\geq0\) is the charged duration of operation \(v\). Its parallel time is the weighted span \[T_\infty(\tau)=\max_{P\in\mathcal P(D_\tau)}\sum_{v\in P}w(v).\] For algorithm \(A\), define \[T_A^\infty(\varepsilon;\mathcal I)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}T_\infty(\tau_A(I,\varepsilon)).\] With unit operation weights this equals the maximum number of causally sequential operations, not total work.
assumptions_latex: \(D_\tau\) is acyclic and contains every charged operation preceding the output.
Each operation has a nonnegative model weight \(w(v)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures critical-path depth in an idealized parallel execution DAG.

notation.meaning: Causal execution directed acyclic graph.
Set of directed paths in the execution graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Latency Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every valid-output causal path contains an unavoidable communication chain, elapsed time is at least the smallest accumulated duration lower bound among those chains; in particular, R sequential communications of latency at least lambda_min require at least R times lambda_min.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_\tau\) be the causal graph of a timed execution \(\tau\), and let \(\lambda(v)\geq0\) be a lower bound on the actual elapsed duration of each communication operation \(v\). Let \(\mathcal C_\varepsilon\) be a family of directed communication chains such that every causal path producing an \(\varepsilon\)-valid output contains at least one \(C\in\mathcal C_\varepsilon\). Because causally ordered operations cannot overlap, \[T_{\mathrm{wall}}(\tau)\geq\min_{C\in\mathcal C_\varepsilon}\sum_{v\in C}\lambda(v).\] In particular, if every such chain contains at least \(R_\varepsilon\) causally sequential communication operations and \(\lambda(v)\geq\lambda_{\min}\) for each of them, then \[T_{\mathrm{wall}}(\tau)\geq R_\varepsilon\lambda_{\min}.\] Concurrent local computation cannot reduce this causal latency term.
assumptions_latex: Every causal path leading to a valid output contains at least one chain \(C\in\mathcal C_\varepsilon\).
For every communication operation \(v\), its actual elapsed duration is at least \(\lambda(v)\geq0\).
Operations on a directed causal chain cannot overlap in time.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bounds completion time using unavoidable causal communication chains.

notation.meaning: Family of communication chains such that every valid-output causal path contains at least one member.
Lower bound on the elapsed duration of communication operation v.
Necessary number of causally sequential communication rounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Overhead
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronization overhead may be measured either as total worker waiting plus separately charged barrier service or as the sum of maximum individual waiting at each barrier; neither convention alone determines global critical-path overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider barriers \(k=1,\ldots,K\) with finite participant sets \(W_k\). Let \(a_{ik}\) be worker \(i\)'s arrival time, let \(r_k\geq\max_{i\in W_k}a_{ik}\) be the release time, and let \(s_k\geq0\) be a separately charged service cost not already included in the waiting intervals. Define aggregate worker-time synchronization overhead by \[H_{\mathrm{sync}}^{\mathrm{agg}}(\tau)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(\sum_{i\in W_k}(r_k-a_{ik})+s_k\right).\] A distinct per-barrier maximum-wait measure is \[H_{\mathrm{sync}}^{\max}(\tau)=\sum_{k=1}^{K}\left(\max_{i\in W_k}(r_k-a_{ik})+s_k\right).\] Neither quantity is, without additional execution-path assumptions, identical to the synchronization contribution on the global critical path. The selected convention must accompany every reported value.
assumptions_latex: Each barrier \(k\) has a finite participant set \(W_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Communication complexity of a distributed primal-dual method
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a communication graph. A distributed primal-dual algorithm \(\mathcal A\) generates iterates and, during round \(t\), transmits messages \(m_{e,t}\) over directed edge uses \(e\). Let \(C(z)\) be a prescribed accuracy certificate and \(\varepsilon\) its target.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous or explicitly round-indexed distributed methods; rounds, messages, scalars, and bits are distinguished cost measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The communication stopping time is \(T_\varepsilon=\inf\{t\in\mathbb N:C(z^t)\leq\varepsilon\}\). The round complexity is \(R_\varepsilon=T_\varepsilon\); the message complexity is \(M_\varepsilon=\sum_{t=1}^{T_\varepsilon}\sum_e\mathbf1\{m_{e,t}\text{ is sent}\}\); the scalar complexity is \(S_\varepsilon=\sum_{t=1}^{T_\varepsilon}\sum_e\dim(m_{e,t})\); and, under an encoding with length \(\ell(m)\), the bit complexity is \(B_\varepsilon=\sum_{t=1}^{T_\varepsilon}\sum_e\ell(m_{e,t})\). These quantities form the communication-complexity profile \(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon(\mathcal A,G)=(R_\varepsilon,M_\varepsilon,S_\varepsilon,B_\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication complexity is the cost incurred before the first iterate satisfying the declared accuracy certificate. Its profile records four noninterchangeable quantities: elapsed communication rounds, transmitted messages, transmitted scalar coordinates, and encoded bits. The graph, scheduling convention, message dimension, encoding, and certificate are part of the definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak C_\varepsilon(\mathcal A,G)=(R_\varepsilon,M_\varepsilon,S_\varepsilon,B_\varepsilon)\) with every component accumulated through \(T_\varepsilon\).
special_cases_latex: If every active directed edge sends one \(d\)-vector per round, then \(S_\varepsilon=dM_\varepsilon\).
If all \(|E|\) undirected edges are used in both directions every round, then \(M_\varepsilon=2|E|R_\varepsilon\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Round complexity alone does not determine bit complexity without a communication and encoding model.
Local computation and oracle calls are excluded unless incorporated as separate coordinates of a broader cost profile.
boundary_notes: For asynchronous algorithms, a round must be defined through epochs, causal depth, or another explicit convention.
Infinite-precision real messages have no finite bit cost without a quantization model.

Uniform-Quantization Accuracy–Bit Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform coordinate quantization has logarithmic payload cost in inverse distortion and Euclidean distortion proportional to the square root of dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For v\in[-R,R]^d, choose N=\lceil2R/\Delta\rceil+1 equally spaced scalar levels on [-R,R] and quantize each coordinate to a nearest level. Then the spacing is at most \Delta and \[\|Q(v)-v\|_2\le\frac{\sqrt d\,\Delta}{2}.\] A fixed-length coordinate index uses \[b_{\rm pay}=d\lceil\log_2N\rceil\] bits. For M_T such messages and h charged overhead bits per message, \[B_T=M_T\bigl(d\lceil\log_2N\rceil+h\bigr).\]
assumptions_latex: Every coordinate lies in \([-R,R]\).
The declared N-level nearest-neighbor uniform quantizer is used.
Fixed-length indices and h overhead bits per message are charged.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete dimension, distortion, and fixed-length payload accounting.

knowledge_statements.title: Compression Bit Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total transmitted-bit accounting for achieving a prescribed optimization accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose round \(k\) transmits \(m_k\) compressed vectors and the \(j\)-th transmitted vector in that round has code length \(b_{k,j}\) bits. If an algorithm guarantees an error measure \(E_K\leq\varepsilon\) after \(K(\varepsilon)\) rounds, then its total payload-bit complexity is \[B(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_k}b_{k,j}.\] If \(m_k=m\), every code length satisfies \(b_{k,j}\leq b\), and \(K(\varepsilon)\leq C\varepsilon^{-p}\), then \(B(\varepsilon)\leq mbC\varepsilon^{-p}\). Protocol overhead must either be included in the code lengths or reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bit complexity sums the actual lengths of all transmitted codes until the target accuracy is reached. Uniform upper bounds multiply vectors per round, bits per vector, and round complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(E_{K(\varepsilon)}\leq\varepsilon\)
Round \(k\) transmits \(m_k\) vectors with code lengths \(b_{k,j}\)
Protocol overhead is either included in \(b_{k,j}\) or explicitly excluded
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m_k}b_{k,j}\), and under the uniform bounds \(B(\varepsilon)\leq mbC\varepsilon^{-p}\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a distributed algorithm produce a declared error \(\mathcal E_K\) after \(K\) iterations. At iteration \(k\), directed link \((j,i)\) transmits a codeword of length \(b_{ij}^k\in\mathbb N_0\). Let \(E_k\) be the set of links used at that iteration.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case or expected end-to-end communication complexity measured in encoded bits; local computation and protocol headers are excluded unless explicitly included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The compression bit complexity for target accuracy \(\varepsilon>0\) is \(\mathsf B(\varepsilon)=\inf\{\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{(j,i)\in E_k}b_{ij}^k:K\in\mathbb N,\ \mathcal E_K\le\varepsilon\}\), where the admissible algorithms, encoders, and parameter schedules are fixed or explicitly quantified. For randomized schemes, expected bit complexity replaces the sum by its expectation and the accuracy condition must use a matching expectation or probability criterion. If no finite run reaches the target, \(\mathsf B(\varepsilon)=+\infty\). Per-agent, per-link, and maximum-message complexities are different metrics and must be named separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compression bit complexity is the minimum total encoded message length needed to reach a declared target error. It sums bits over all active links and iterations, with the algorithmic and coding class fixed or explicitly quantified. For randomized communication, both the bit total and accuracy criterion must state whether they are expected or high probability. Unattainable accuracy has infinite bit complexity.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If every active message uses exactly \(b\) bits, then \(\mathsf B(\varepsilon)=b\inf\{\sum_{k<K}|E_k|:\mathcal E_K\le\varepsilon\}\).
special_cases_latex: For a fixed graph used every round with \(|E|\) directed links and \(b_k\) bits per message, total bits through round \(K\) equal \(|E|\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}b_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A comparison of iteration counts alone does not determine bit complexity when message lengths differ.
boundary_notes: Encoding metadata, acknowledgments, and retransmissions are excluded unless incorporated into \(b_{ij}^k\).
Real-number oracle communication has no finite bit count without an encoding model.

knowledge_statements.title: Federated-Averaging Communication Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a convergence round bound, total messages scale with participating clients per round, while total local oracle calls also scale with each client's local-step count.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(\varepsilon)=\min\{R:\mathcal{E}(x^R)\le\varepsilon\}\). Under the stated message model, reaching accuracy \(\varepsilon\) uses \(R(\varepsilon)\) synchronization rounds, \[M(\varepsilon)=2\sum_{t=0}^{R(\varepsilon)-1}m_t\] client messages, equivalently \(dM(\varepsilon)\) transmitted scalar coordinates, and \[N(\varepsilon)=\sum_{t=0}^{R(\varepsilon)-1}\sum_{i\in S_t}K_{i,t}\] local oracle calls. A convergence theorem supplies \(R(\varepsilon)\); these identities expose the tradeoff between local work, participation, and communication.
assumptions_latex: One communication round broadcasts one \(d\)-dimensional server model and receives one \(d\)-dimensional response from each of \(m_t\) participating clients.
An accuracy criterion \(\mathcal{E}(x)\le\varepsilon\) and a convergence guarantee determining \(R(\varepsilon)\) are fixed.
Client \(i\) performs \(K_{i,t}\) local oracle calls in round \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The round complexity is \(R(\varepsilon)\), the client-message complexity is \(2\sum_{t<R(\varepsilon)}m_t\), and the local-oracle complexity is \(\sum_{t<R(\varepsilon)}\sum_{i\in S_t}K_{i,t}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource accounting separated from any assumption-dependent convergence rate.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an algorithm produce server iterates \(x_0,x_1,\ldots\), with one broadcast-and-aggregate exchange per round. Let \(\mathcal E(x)\ge0\) be a prescribed optimization error or stationarity criterion and let \(K_t\) and \(|S_t|\) denote local work and participation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An accuracy-indexed complexity definition, not a particular convergence-rate theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), the communication-round complexity is \(R_{\mathcal E}(\varepsilon)=\inf\{R\in\mathbb N:\mathbb E[\mathcal E(x_R)]\le\varepsilon\}\), with value \(+\infty\) if the set is empty. The associated client-update work is \(W(\varepsilon)=\sum_{t=0}^{R_{\mathcal E}(\varepsilon)-1}\sum_{i\in S_t}K_{t,i}\), and a model-vector transmission count may be recorded as \(C(\varepsilon)=\sum_{t<R_{\mathcal E}(\varepsilon)}(c_t^{\rm down}+c_t^{\rm up})\). A communication-computation-participation tradeoff is the dependence of these quantities on \(K_{t,i}\), \(|S_t|\), sampling, and the chosen accuracy criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication complexity is the smallest number of server rounds needed to make a specified expected error no larger than the target tolerance. Local update work and transmitted model vectors are separate resource measures, so changing local epochs or participation may improve one measure while worsening another.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathcal E}(\varepsilon)=\inf\{R:\mathbb E[\mathcal E(x_R)]\le\varepsilon\}\), accompanied by separately reported local-work and transmission counts.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A high-probability version replaces the expectation condition by \(\Pr(\mathcal E(x_R)\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\).
special_cases_latex: For smooth nonconvex objectives, \(\mathcal E(x)=\|\nabla F(x)\|^2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Round complexity alone does not determine total bandwidth because participation and message size may vary by round.
boundary_notes: Wall-clock time additionally depends on latency, parallelism, stragglers, and hardware.
The definition does not supply a rate or assert that increasing local work reduces communication.
